## What this file checks

One thing, in isolation: what happens to LaTeX that pandoc **forwards** rather
than parses.

Pandoc turns markdown it understands into a format-neutral document and writes
each output format from that, so markdown emphasis becomes the right thing in
every format. LaTeX written out by hand is not parsed at all. It is copied into
the LaTeX output verbatim and dropped from every other format, silently and with
no error.

The two constructs below fail in **opposite** directions, which is why they are
here rather than in the four full fixtures: one is lost by Typst and the other by
LaTeX, so neither route can be called the good one.

Every marker below is a nonsense word that appears nowhere else in this file. A
needle that also occurs in the prose beside the construct cannot fail, which has
already happened here twice -- see the note in `ci/assert-renders.py`.

## Raw LaTeX outside maths

A footnote written as raw LaTeX, which pandoc forwards
verbatim.\footnote{RTFN -- this note reaches the LaTeX PDF and nothing else.}

The same thing written as markdown, which pandoc parses.^[MDFN -- this note
reaches every route.]

Only the second one survives everywhere.

## A literal Greek character inside maths

`$$` is not a shield. `\text{}` inside maths switches back to the text font, so a
literal Greek character there is dropped by LaTeX exactly as it would be in
prose, inside an equation that otherwise typesets perfectly:

$$
\theta_{\mathrm{TXTGRK}} = \text{α}
$$

Written as a command rather than as a literal character, it renders everywhere:

$$
\theta_{\mathrm{CMDGRK}} = \alpha
$$

## What you should see

Both equations appear in all three outputs, and both subscripts with them. The
Greek letter is present in the Typst PDF and the HTML but missing from the first
equation in the LaTeX PDF, which reports nothing about having dropped it.

Of the two footnotes, the LaTeX PDF has both and the other two routes have only
the markdown one.
